question: Find the equation of the curve passing through $(1,1)$ if the slope of its tangent at any point $(x,y)$ is $$\frac{x^2-y^2}{2xy}.$$ Establish that the resulting differential equation is homogeneous and obtain the required curve by a suitable substitution.
explanation:
Formation of the Differential Equation
The slope of the tangent is $\frac{dy}{dx}$. Hence, $$\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{x^2-y^2}{2xy}=\frac{1-\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)^2}{2\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)}.$$ Thus the right-hand side is a function of $\frac{y}{x}$ only, so the equation is homogeneous.

Substitution Method
Put $$y=vx.$$ Then $$\frac{dy}{dx}=v+x\frac{dv}{dx}.$$ Therefore, $$v+x\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{1-v^2}{2v}.$$ Hence, $$x\frac{dv}{dx}=\frac{1-3v^2}{2v}.$$

Reduction to Variable Separable Form
Separating variables, $$\frac{2v}{1-3v^2}dv=\frac{dx}{x}.$$ Integrating, $$-\frac{1}{3}\log|1-3v^2|=\log|x|+C.$$ Thus, $$\log|1-3v^2|=-3\log|x|+C_1.$$ Hence, after absorbing the non-zero constant, $$1-3v^2=\frac{C}{x^3}.$$ Replacing $v$ by $\frac{y}{x}$ gives $$x^3-3xy^2=C.$$

The curve passes through $(1,1)$, so $$C=1-3=-2.$$

Final Result
The equation of the required curve is $$x^3-3xy^2=-2.$$
